title: Prefer fuller definitions — English Confession 1647: whole Word, chiefly receiving Christ
source_text: LXXXVIII. Itaque magis probamus definitiones illas, quae naturam fidei justificantis plenius & distinctius exponunt & declarant. Qualis est descriptio Fidei quae reperitur in Confessione Anglicana Anni 1647. dum dicit fidem salutarem esse per quam Christianus verum credit quicquid est Verbo Dei revelatum, propter Dei ipsius in Verbo loquentis authoritatem, & differenter agit ac afficitur super singulis quae continet istud Verbum; mandatis scilicet, obsequens, ad minas contremiscens, & amplectens Dei promissiones, tam quae ad hanc vitam, quam quae ad futuram pertinent. Sed fidei illius, praecipuos actus esse, acceptare & recipere Christum, & in eo solo acquiescere ad justificationem, sanctificationem, & vitam aeternam, virtute foederis gratiae.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore we rather approve those definitions which more fully and distinctly set forth and declare the nature of justifying faith. Such is the description of Faith which is found in the English Confession of the Year 1647, when it says that saving faith is that by which a Christian believes as true whatever is revealed by the Word of God, because of the authority of God himself speaking in the Word, and differently acts and is affected upon each of those things which that Word contains; namely, obedient to the commands, trembling at the threatenings, and embracing God's promises, both those which pertain to this life and those which pertain to the future. But that the chief acts of that faith are to accept and receive Christ, and to rest in him alone unto justification, sanctification, and eternal life, by virtue of the covenant of grace.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc prefers fuller, clearer definitions of justifying faith.

English Confession 1647: saving faith believes whatever God reveals, on God’s speaking authority, and is differently moved by each part — obeys commands, trembles at threats, embraces promises for this life and the next.
Chief acts: accept and receive Christ, and rest in him alone for justification, sanctification, and eternal life, by the covenant of grace.
